nodes.panel_description: A wide road descends through black rain toward a timber palisade. Refugees, broken carts, cages, and severe gate towers dwarf the people below.
nodes.text: Three miles from home, Garren finds the road narrowed to a queue and a Crown checkpoint. Soldiers search veterans twice. Captain Orl's sealed packet rests against his ribs, dry as an accusation.

choices.text: Take a place in line before the rain worsens.
Climb the rise and watch first.

nodes.panel_description: The checkpoint lies below high muddy grass. Drainage water cuts along the palisade while clerks and soldiers move beneath rain and black pennants.
nodes.speaker: Garren
nodes.text: The culvert could pass a man, not a wagon. At the awning, a clerk replaces the public notice with a sealed sheet. One lesson, before somebody notices the student.

choices.text: Remember the flooded culvert.
Watch the clerk exchange the orders.

nodes.panel_description: A ground-level view beneath a bowed merchant wagon: axle, boots, mud, a pale hand, and flour leaking from split sacking. Faces remain outside the frame.
nodes.speaker: Tavin
nodes.text: Vale. Keep your eyes on the gate. Red Hollow was arranged, not lost. Orl gave you the proof they are hunting.

choices.text: Call Meret's soldiers.
Push him behind the false floor.
Say he has the wrong veteran.
Make him earn the hiding place.

nodes.panel_description: Portcullis ribs frame an inspection trestle while Tavin kneels under guard beside Sella's wagon. Meret stands upright beneath a narrow awning.
nodes.speaker: Captain Meret
nodes.text: You hand me a signalman before I ask. Efficient. The warrant wants him, anything sealed by Orl, and the man who taught prisoners to confess politely.

choices.text: Answer as a discharged soldier.
Say Orl's packet never left Red Hollow.
Name the flaw in Red Hollow's counterseal.

nodes.panel_description: Portcullis ribs hang over a wet inspection trestle. Meret is a dark upright figure while a soldier's spear tests the wagon canvas above Tavin.
nodes.speaker: Captain Meret
nodes.text: Still watching other people's hands, Vale? The warrant wants an Orl seal and an unnamed signalman. It also remembers what you did for the regiment.

choices.text: Answer as a discharged soldier.
Say Orl's packet never left Red Hollow.
Name the flaw in Red Hollow's counterseal.

nodes.panel_description: Rain pours through the outer gate as the refugee line closes behind Sella's wagon. Meret studies Garren while a distant voice calls his name.
nodes.speaker: Captain Meret
nodes.text: A signalman just mistook you for salvation. Embarrassing for both of you. The warrant wants him, an Orl seal, and any veteran who looks too carefully at the paper.

choices.text: Answer as a discharged soldier.
Say Orl's packet never left Red Hollow.
Name the flaw in Red Hollow's counterseal.

nodes.panel_description: Under the outer gate, wet ledgers share a trestle with confiscated knives. A shape clings beneath Sella's wagon while Meret watches Garren instead.
nodes.speaker: Captain Meret
nodes.text: There is a man under that wagon deciding how expensive your name should become. The warrant wants a signalman, an Orl seal, and someone with your old profession.

choices.text: Answer as a discharged soldier.
Say Orl's packet never left Red Hollow.
Name the flaw in Red Hollow's counterseal.

nodes.panel_description: Sella's wagon wheel is sunk to the hub between sharpened gates. Many hands push while a torn canvas exposes the lines of a false floor and Tavin waits under guard.
nodes.speaker: Sella Venn
nodes.text: You sold the soldiers my passenger and left me the wagon. Generous. There are three people under its papers who cannot survive your next good decision.

choices.text: Promise to get all of them through.
Threaten to expose the false floor.
Pledge Orl's packet as collateral.

nodes.panel_description: Sella's wagon wheel is sunk to the hub between sharpened gates. Pushing hands hide the false floor's open seam while Tavin lies silent beneath worn timber.
nodes.speaker: Sella Venn
nodes.text: Your signalman is under my flour, my dependents are under my papers, and your face has improved the soldiers' curiosity. Which disaster are you buying?

choices.text: Promise to get all of them through.
Threaten to expose the false floor.
Pledge Orl's packet as collateral.

nodes.panel_description: A wagon wheel founders between the gates. The torn canvas reveals a false floor while the refugee line behind it shifts around a man no longer visible.
nodes.speaker: Sella Venn
nodes.text: You left the signalman in a crowd that sells names for dry socks. Sensible. Now decide whether the people in my wagon deserve the same economy.

choices.text: Promise to get all of them through.
Threaten to expose the false floor.
Pledge Orl's packet as collateral.

nodes.panel_description: The merchant wagon leans over a wheel buried in mud. Beneath it, a pale hand waits beside the false floor while soldiers gather at both gates.
nodes.speaker: Sella Venn
nodes.text: Tavin paid for canvas and silence. You charged him again for hope. I admire a man who can rob a customer without moving his hands.

choices.text: Promise to get all of them through.
Threaten to expose the false floor.
Pledge Orl's packet as collateral.

nodes.panel_description: The checkpoint bell rings once above a slamming gate. Tavin is dragged toward a hanging cage as refugees compress around Sella's stranded wagon.
nodes.text: The bar falls. Tavin is already in Meret's hands, close enough to accuse Garren and frightened enough to improve the story.

choices.text: Face the sealed courtyard.

nodes.panel_description: A gate slams across the road while soldiers close a ring around the wagons. Beneath Sella's false floor, Tavin presses one hand against the timber.
nodes.text: The bar falls. Tavin remains hidden, which now means every person near the wagon is part of the hiding place.

choices.text: Face the sealed courtyard.

nodes.panel_description: The gate shuts on a packed refugee line. A lone figure moves between wagons while soldiers turn pikes inward and Sella's wheel remains buried.
nodes.text: The bar falls. Tavin has vanished into the crowd. Somewhere behind Garren, a man with nothing left to protect is deciding when to shout.

choices.text: Face the sealed courtyard.

nodes.panel_description: Soldiers seal the courtyard around a stranded wagon. A hand beneath the axle loosens its grip as the crowd pushes against the closing line.
nodes.text: The bar falls. Tavin still has information to sell and Garren's name to sweeten the price.

choices.text: Face the sealed courtyard.

nodes.panel_description: A gate slams shut beneath a severed bell note. Refugees are compressed among wagons while soldiers close a ring; rain and palisade dominate every figure.
nodes.speaker: Captain Meret
nodes.text: This order left before any messenger saw you. It names the signalman, Orl's packet, and the old supply books. Either the Crown has learned prophecy, or someone here has been sold twice.

choices.text: Use the culvert to buy a private minute.
Follow the clerk's paper trail.
Take the bell rope and steady the crowd.
Make Sella's wagon look already searched.
Make Meret read the order aloud.

nodes.panel_description: Wet possessions cover a scarred table beneath the main awning. Sealed papers lie between a knife and ink pot while a brazier smokes in the rain; only hands and sleeves enter the frame.
nodes.speaker: Garren
nodes.text: Orl addressed the packet to me. Inside, his note wraps a pressure-copy of the Red Hollow countermand. Its crooked counterseal has a younger twin on Meret's warrant. One proof can point four ways and survive none of them alone.

choices.text: Follow the crossed-out supply books.
Hear Tavin before fear edits him.
Honor Sella's claim before the search.
Put Meret's mark beside the counterseal.

nodes.panel_description: A cramped timber loft holds shelves of swollen ledgers and ration bowls catching roof leaks. One open folio is crossed by a hard shaft of gray light; the clerk waits beside the ladder.
nodes.speaker: Garren
nodes.text: Three days before Red Hollow, a clerk killed the regiment with one ruled line. Vale's companies vanish from the ration roll. A replacement detail eats their bread and inherits their courier serial.

choices.text: Steal the original folio.
Make a precise copy of the entries.
Memorize the serials and leave no gap.

nodes.panel_description: In the clerk's leaking loft, Meret stands with her back to the ladder while Garren studies a crossed-out regiment and a replacement ration detail in the open folio.
nodes.speaker: Captain Meret
nodes.text: The stores moved three days before the battle. I signed couriers, not graves. That distinction was more comforting before you found the arithmetic.

choices.text: Let Meret remove the folio under seal.
Copy the entries beneath her hand.
Commit the serials to memory.

nodes.panel_description: A narrow service passage runs between flooded culvert stones and hanging cages. Tavin is broken into reflections by rising water and iron bars; no face is clear.
nodes.speaker: Tavin
nodes.text: I saw the countermand arrive. They ordered me to keep the beacon dark. I obeyed for twelve minutes, lit it too late, gave Sella the courier strap, and ran before the dead could ask why.

conditional_text.text: Meret orders the cage carried to the service passage. Tavin can answer through iron, but he cannot leave it.
Sella slips Tavin from beneath the false floor while the search turns toward the outer wagons.
Tavin comes out only after Garren lets him keep the wagon between himself and Meret's soldiers.

choices.text: Offer terms and accept an imperfect witness.
Force him through the sequence again.
Place him in Meret's custody for formal testimony.

nodes.panel_description: Runoff floods the passage behind the cages. A ration serial lies between Garren and Tavin, reached through bars, beneath canvas, or in one brief gap in the crowd.
nodes.speaker: Tavin
nodes.text: The serial belonged to the courier who brought the countermand. Tavin kept the beacon dark for twelve minutes, lit it too late, gave Sella the stamped strap, and ran from the answer.

conditional_text.text: Meret permits one interview through the cage bars. The proof reaches Tavin; freedom does not.
Sella brings Tavin from beneath the false floor to the flooded passage, then hides him there again.
Tavin leaves the wagon's shadow only after Garren shows him the serial. He keeps one path back to hiding open.

Garren passes the serial through the refugee queue as a summons only a signalman would recognize. Tavin returns for this account and no bargain more; without formal protection, he vanishes into the crowd again.

choices.text: Offer terms and accept an imperfect witness.
Force him through the sequence again.
Place him in Meret's custody for formal testimony.

nodes.panel_description: Inside Sella's tilted wagon, crates, flour dust, wet blankets, and merchant papers frame a lifted false floor. A stamped leather strap lies small against the worn timber.
nodes.speaker: Sella Venn
nodes.text: I told the checkpoint a valuable deserter was coming. I meant to buy safe passage, not an execution. Then Tavin arrived with this strap and made the difference inconvenient.

choices.text: Accept her terms and renew the bargain.
Use her tip to take the strap.
Expose her to Tavin and Meret.

nodes.panel_description: The wagon's false floor stands open between Tavin's wet boots and Sella's flour sacks. The courier strap rests apart from both of them while hidden dependents hold still beneath merchant papers.
nodes.speaker: Sella Venn
nodes.text: He gave me the strap. I sold the checkpoint a rumor about a valuable deserter before I learned their warrant meant a corpse. Pricing a betrayal does not make it less personal, but it does make it legible.

choices.text: Accept her terms and renew the bargain.
Use her tip to take the strap.
Expose her to Tavin and Meret.

nodes.panel_description: Meret's severe room above the gate has a dry map wall, a folded uniform, and one narrow window over the wet crowd. The current warrant is held near an unlit stove; both figures face away.
nodes.speaker: Captain Meret
nodes.text: I authenticated the Red Hollow courier chain. This warrant carries the same flawed counterseal and orders every seized proof burned. I kept that clause from my soldiers. Delay is the uniform cowardice wears on good days.

choices.text: Share Orl's proof and ask her to preserve the chain.
Blackmail her signature into service.
Offer silence for people and records leaving.

nodes.panel_description: Above the gate, Sella's stamped strap and Meret's warrant lie beneath a dry map wall. The crowd is visible through one narrow window while the unlit stove waits beside the papers.
nodes.speaker: Captain Meret
nodes.text: Venn brought you a courier's strap and a betrayal. I can match the first to this warrant because I authenticated the Red Hollow chain. The order says to burn both after seizure. My soldiers have not read that line yet.

choices.text: Share one proof and ask her to preserve the chain.
Blackmail her signature into service.
Offer silence for people and records leaving.

nodes.panel_description: Under a sagging supply canvas, Orl's packet, a ration folio in its chosen form, and the space reserved for Tavin's account sit on an upturned crate. No courier strap or current warrant joins them.
nodes.speaker: Garren
nodes.text: The ration record proves foreknowledge. Tavin supplies the twelve missing minutes. Sella still has the courier strap, and Meret's present warrant remains beyond reach. The case has a spine and two empty ribs.

choices.text: Put the available case in Meret's chain.
Give the available case to Tavin.
Put the available case under Sella's canvas.
Split the packet and ration proof.
Build a decoy and hide the strongest proof with Tavin.

nodes.panel_description: Beneath wet supply canvas, Tavin's place faces the courier strap on an upturned crate beside Orl's packet. Empty boards mark the absent ration folio and warrant.
nodes.speaker: Garren
nodes.text: Tavin's account joins the courier strap to Orl's copy. The ration folio remains in the loft and Meret's warrant remains upstairs. Three people can tell parts of the truth; none can yet prove the whole.

choices.text: Put the available case in Meret's chain.
Give the available case to Tavin.
Put the available case under Sella's canvas.
Split the packet and courier proof.
Build a decoy and hide the strongest proof with Tavin.

nodes.panel_description: A courier strap, Orl's packet under Sella's claim, and a copy or guarded view of Meret's warrant occupy separate corners of an upturned crate. The folio and witness place are empty.
nodes.speaker: Garren
nodes.text: The strap binds Orl's copy to the current warrant. No ration folio proves when the betrayal began, and Tavin's confession remains unheard. The case can travel, but it cannot yet stand still under questioning.

choices.text: Put the available case in Meret's chain.
Give the available case to Tavin.
Keep the available case under Sella's canvas.
Split the packet, strap, and warrant.
Build a decoy and leave the strongest proof with Sella.

nodes.panel_description: Meret's warrant and the ration evidence share a crate beneath the supply canvas while Orl's packet rests under official custody. Empty places remain for Tavin and Sella's courier strap.
nodes.speaker: Garren
nodes.text: Meret can authenticate the warrant and the ration record proves preparation. Tavin has not given his twelve minutes, and Sella's strap remains hidden. The official chain is strong enough to bury itself neatly.

choices.text: Keep the available case in Meret's chain.
Give the available case to Tavin.
Put the available case under Sella's canvas.
Split the packet, ration proof, and warrant.
Build a decoy and leave the strongest proof with Meret.

nodes.panel_description: Hard rain bows a supply canvas over an upturned crate. The chosen bundle, divided proofs, or decoy now sits beneath three withdrawing sets of hands; absent evidence leaves visible gaps.
nodes.speaker: Garren
nodes.text: No route yielded everything. What survived now belongs to a person, several roads, or a lie built to protect the rest. The empty spaces are evidence too. For once, Garren refuses to fill them with whatever answer fear would accept.

choices.text: Face the order that came for all of it.

nodes.panel_description: The courtyard splits around an opening gate and a panicked crowd. A cage line, Sella's wagon, a burning ledger basket, and collapsing ranks of soldiers remain small beneath the palisade.
nodes.speaker: Captain Meret
nodes.text: The superior's order is short enough for frightened men: execute the signalman, burn the ledger, seize Venn's wagon, clear the refugees. Meret's delay is over. Sella puts one hand on the reins.

conditional_text.text: Tavin grips the cage bars while a clerk reads the line that will kill him.
Tavin waits beneath the wagon canvas, close enough to hear soldiers search for his body.
Tavin is absent. The order names a man no one in the courtyard can point to without lying.
Tavin holds at the edge of his hiding place, with Garren's name ready for whichever side reaches him first.
Tavin stands inside Meret's guarded chain, protected by a false transfer that her superior can still revoke.
Tavin is already beyond the checkpoint, leaving the execution line with no body to claim.

choices.text: Hold Meret's line while she falsifies the count.
Get Tavin through the culvert.
Force Sella's wagon through the opening.
Destroy the warrant where the crowd can hear it.

nodes.panel_description: Meret's soldiers hold a narrow line before the opening gate while refugees sit under spear watch. Behind the line, one seizure ledger receives a deliberate false count.
nodes.speaker: Captain Meret
nodes.text: Meret writes fewer prisoners than stand in the rain. Whether she acts from trust, guilt, or fear of Garren's leverage, one soldier sees the lie and lowers his pike. The refugees live, but the road keeps them.

choices.text: Cross the threshold she bought.

nodes.panel_description: Floodwater surges through the opened culvert beneath the wall. Tavin disappears as a reflection while a young soldier turns his pike away from the fleeing shadow.
nodes.speaker: Tavin
nodes.text: Garren gets Tavin through the collapsing guard line and into the floodwater. If Tavin trusted him, it is rescue. If fear won, it is merely the first escape that came with a witness. A soldier refuses the order and inherits the punishment.

choices.text: Cross before the culvert is found.

nodes.panel_description: Sella's wagon tears through a broken pike line as refugees scatter from its wheels. Hidden dependents crouch beneath black canvas; mud and blood mark the opening it leaves.
nodes.speaker: Sella Venn
nodes.text: The wagon passes because Garren makes other bodies yield first. Sella's dependents leave the cage-yard, and her license will be ash by morning. A promise is kept with somebody else's bruises.

choices.text: Follow the wagon's costly opening.

nodes.panel_description: The current warrant tears above a smoking ledger basket while soldiers and refugees crowd close enough to hear every clause. The gate line folds into disorder behind it.
nodes.speaker: Garren
nodes.text: Garren reads the destruction clause aloud, then tears the warrant through Meret's mark. The crowd learns enough to become dangerous and not enough to become safe. The gate opens as a riot, not an answer.

choices.text: Walk through what the words broke.

nodes.panel_description: The checkpoint gate stands half-open onto drowned fields at gray dawn. Roads divide toward town, a marsh chapel, and the merchant track; discarded military insignia lies alone in the mud.
nodes.speaker: Garren
nodes.text: The gate has opened, but the case has not become innocent. Garren can choose who carries what survived, and therefore what kind of danger it becomes. That choice will be his oath; no speech can improve it.

choices.text: Place the case in Meret's hidden record.
Carry it toward the ruined chapel with Tavin.
Put it into Sella's trade network.
Burn the corroboration still within reach.

nodes.panel_description: An empty records room after rain, with one false ledger entry drying beside a locked evidence box while the gate road shows through a narrow window.
nodes.text: In Meret's empty records room, rain ticks from the rafters. She falsifies the seizure ledger and writes Garren in as a Crown informant. What reached her goes into a locked evidence box; what did not stays beyond her reach. He keeps a future chance at truth by helping the present lie survive.

conditional_text.text: The available case fits inside Meret's chain, authentic enough to reopen and just as easy to bury.
Meret locks away only her share. The divided copies remain on roads she cannot close without exposing why they matter.
Tavin still holds the assembled case; Meret records only the proof that actually reached her and does not pretend the box is fuller.
Sella still holds the assembled case; Meret's box receives only its surviving official fragment.
The decoy enters Meret's record. The strongest proof remains with the custodian chosen beneath the supply canvas.
Meret accepts the case without a private bargain between them. Garren gives an institution custody and receives no promise that its captain will choose him over it.
Meret leaves the informant line unsigned and keeps the key herself. It is trust of a narrow sort: each can ruin the other by speaking too soon.
Meret places one deliberate error in Garren's description. Their silence bargain becomes a small escape hatch between two practiced liars.
Meret writes Garren's full name, former trade, and usefulness for her superiors. Blackmail bought the box; it also bought her a weapon.
Tavin remains behind the bars, alive and entered as a common deserter so the warrant does not learn what he witnessed.
Tavin becomes a protected courier in the false ledger, a prisoner whose cage now has paperwork facing both ways.
Meret lists Tavin as drowned in the culvert. The lie protects his body and gives her soldiers a grave to search.
Tavin survives in the wagon's shadow while Meret records an empty cage and chooses not to count the breathing beneath the canvas.
No one at the gate can say where Tavin went. Meret turns that absence into an official death and Garren lets her.
Sella's wagon is already beyond the wall; the kept bargain leaves Garren owing her no apology, only future trouble.
Meret seizes Sella's license instead of her dependents. The broken promise survives as a debt Sella can name later.
Sella leaves with Garren's bargain still unpaid. Meret's quiet record protects people, not his word.
Sella accepts no part in the official fiction. She remembers only that Garren found shelter inside the institution searching her wagon.
The refugees live under spear watch until another clerk can invent permission for mercy.
A young soldier is taken for refusing the order. His name is the one Meret cannot remove from the morning report.
The road opens, but the wounded remain beside the gate while the false ledger calls the passage orderly.
The torn warrant has already taught the crowd too much. Meret can preserve a private case, not restore obedience.

nodes.panel_description: A ruined chapel above a flooded marsh, with two distant figures approaching while checkpoint torches spread behind them like a search line.
nodes.text: Garren and Tavin cross the marsh toward a chapel with half a roof and a network that still remembers how to print accusations. The checkpoint torches divide behind them. Garren has joined himself to a compromised witness instead of extracting the useful facts and walking away. The truth has a voice now, and everyone who helped it escape can be punished.

conditional_text.text: Tavin carries the available case beside his own account; proof and witness can be hunted together.
Only one divided share goes toward the chapel. Other copies survive on roads neither fugitive controls.
Meret keeps the assembled proof. Garren and Tavin carry testimony without the documents that might make strangers believe it.
Sella keeps the assembled proof. The chapel receives a witness while the documents travel at a merchant's pace and price.
The decoy draws the first search. The strongest proof follows whichever hand received it beneath the supply canvas.
The ration arithmetic proves preparation and Tavin supplies the missing minutes; the courier strap and current warrant are still absent.
The stamped strap joins Tavin's account to Orl's copy; no ration folio or current warrant travels with them.
The strap and warrant can expose the present hunt, but no ration record proves when the sacrifice began and Tavin was not first heard cleanly.
The ration record and warrant carry official weight; Sella's strap is absent and Tavin's account entered the case late, if at all.
Tavin tells the chapel about the twelve dark minutes, including the part that condemns him. Garren earned a usable confession by accepting an imperfect man.
Tavin gives the cleaner accusation and keeps one lie for protection. Garren's old methods have preserved a witness who may expose him first.
Tavin reaches the chapel with an incomplete account. The printers will have a living witness and no honest certainty about his worst twelve minutes.
Sella's people are already moving. The kept bargain becomes a covert road the fugitives may use once before its price changes.
Sella gives the pursuit their direction before dawn. A broken promise is useful merchandise when soldiers are buying.
Garren leaves Sella with an unpaid promise at the gate. The chapel will hear about that debt before it hears his defense.
Sella owes the fugitives no road, silence, or warning. Their manhunt begins without a merchant's shelter.
The refugees remain penned behind Meret's line while the two men use the freedom denied to them.
The soldier who looked away is arrested before Garren reaches the reeds. Their escape has already found its first substitute prisoner.
Sella's opening leaves bruised refugees in the mud and a cleaner trail for the pursuit to follow.
The riot carries fragments of the warrant into town ahead of them. The truth is no longer theirs to time, only to survive.

nodes.panel_description: A merchant wagon crossing a flooded causeway at dawn, cargo lashed beneath black canvas while the checkpoint shrinks behind it and several roads vanish into fog.
nodes.text: Sella's wagon reaches the flooded causeway with people hidden beneath the cargo and Garren riding beside a woman who prices every rescue. Her network has buyers, printers, smugglers, and rivals, not a neutral public. Garren preserves the case by surrendering control of when it moves and whom it wounds. The truth survives the gate; it becomes merchandise before it becomes justice.

conditional_text.text: The available proofs travel in separate canvas compartments, all inside Sella's network and none inside Garren's control.
Sella carries only one divided share. Other pieces take roads she can bargain with but cannot wholly command.
Meret keeps the assembled case. Sella sells routes, rumor, and access rather than documents she never received.
Tavin keeps the assembled case. Sella's network transports the danger without owning its proof.
The decoy takes the obvious hiding place. Whatever stronger proof reached Sella is buried deeper; nothing absent appears beneath the canvas.
The ration record and Tavin's account can show preparation; the courier strap and current warrant never joined the case.
Tavin's account and the courier strap can corroborate the countermand; the ration folio and warrant remain beyond the network.
The strap and warrant expose the present cover-up, but the network has no ration folio and no tested witness account.
The ration folio and warrant carry official weight; the strap and a clean confession remain missing.
Garren kept the bargain in public. Sella treats him as a partner, which means she tells him the price before taking it.
Garren broke the bargain and still needs her roads. Sella accepts the arrangement as a debt she intends to reverse with interest.
The original bargain remains unpaid. Every mile the wagon travels makes Garren's word more expensive.
No promise softens the transaction. Sella names Garren cargo until his usefulness exceeds his weight.
Tavin stays in Meret's cage while the wagon leaves. Sella will trade for him only if a living witness becomes worth more than a safe route.
Tavin remains under Meret's reluctant protection, separated from the proof that may eventually require his voice.
Tavin is already beyond the culvert. Sella sends one road-sign toward the chapel and charges the favor to Garren.
Tavin rides beneath the false floor, close enough to hear Sella discuss which version of his confession will sell.
Tavin is absent from the wagon. His knowledge survives only in what he already said and what other people choose to repeat.
The wagon escapes while the refugees remain behind the pikes. Sella calls that arithmetic; Garren has no kinder total.
A soldier takes the punishment for looking away. His refusal becomes the first secret Sella's network can sell back to the garrison.
Blood marks the wheel ruts behind them. The dependents are safe because strangers were forced aside.
The riot sends rumor down every road before Sella can portion it. Her advantage is reduced to knowing which lie will arrive second.

nodes.panel_description: A brazier overturned in rain, with black paper scraps dissolving into mud while refugees and soldiers face the same empty gate.
nodes.text: Garren feeds the corroboration still within reach to the brazier and watches rain turn ash into black paste. The search loses its immediate prize, but spoken knowledge and witnessed defiance remain. He chooses living bodies over the dead's claim and names the act correctly: destruction, not neutrality. The Crown will remember that he can make dangerous truth disappear.

conditional_text.text: Meret's assembled case is beyond the flame. Garren burns his notes and seal rubbings, not the proof already inside her chain.
Tavin's assembled case is beyond the flame. Garren destroys only what remained in his own keeping.
Sella's assembled case is beyond the flame. The fire protects her wagon from what Garren still carried, not from what he already entrusted to it.
Garren burns his divided share. Copies already sent elsewhere survive him and may surface without his consent.
The decoy burns convincingly. The strongest proof remains with the hand chosen beneath the supply canvas.
Tavin knows his honest account has lost its nearest corroboration. He leaves without forgiveness and carries the twelve dark minutes in his own name.
Tavin laughs once and tells the nearest soldiers that Garren has burned the proof after teaching him what to confess. The accusation survives because coercion gave it a voice.
Tavin's account remains incomplete or unheard. The flames erase documents more thoroughly than they erase his suspicion.
Sella takes her people through the opening and lets the fire remove one reason to search them. The kept promise does not make her grateful.
Sella watches Garren destroy what he once used against her. The broken bargain remains; only its collateral changes.
Garren's promise to Sella remains unpaid after the ash settles. Burning evidence cannot settle a human debt.
Sella owes the fire no loyalty. She memorizes who ordered it and who obeyed, because information need not be written to become merchandise.
Tavin watches from the cage while soldiers warm their hands over the end of his case.
Tavin survives under Meret's protection, carrying testimony that the official record can now dismiss as a prisoner's grievance.
Tavin is already beyond the wall. The fire cannot reach his voice, only the proof that might have supported it.
Tavin slips away beneath canvas and rain. Whether he condemns Garren later depends on which memory frightens him more.
Tavin is absent when the papers burn. Garren cannot know whether he has protected a fugitive or erased a missing man's only defense.
The refugees may leave only after the search finds nothing worth holding them for; the hours under pikes remain theirs to carry.
The refusing soldier remains under arrest even after the order loses its evidence. Obedience needs no proof to punish hesitation.
The wounded gain an open road and no explanation for why their blood purchased it.
The crowd already heard the warrant before it tore. Fire can destroy paper, not public knowledge, and the riot carries that difference into town.
